About

As a Frontend-focused Full-Stack Developer, I build scalable and user-centric web applications using React, Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, with strong foundations in Node.js and APIs. I focus on performance, responsive design, and cross-browser compatibility to deliver reliable digital experiences.

At RagaAI, I worked on LLM, agentic, and computer vision platforms, contributing to AI-driven interfaces and data visualization using Plotly, Chart.js, and Canvas. My frontend workflow includes Storybook and Vitest for component-driven development and maintainable design systems.

Previously at CedCommerce, I contributed to large-scale e-commerce applications, building analytics interfaces and customer-facing features used by thousands of merchants, while collaborating closely with backend teams to deliver seamless experiences.

I stay aligned with Generative AI, LLM, and RAG ecosystems, focusing on how modern AI capabilities can translate into practical and intuitive UIs. I follow Agile methodologies, write clean and maintainable code, and continuously upskill with emerging technologies.

I hold a Master of Computer Applications from KNIT, which has strengthened my problem-solving and software development foundation.

Open to frontend and AI-focused roles where I can combine full-stack understanding with impactful UI development.

    What is an "AI Frontend Engineer"?

    My LinkedIn title is now "AI Frontend Engineer", some people have asked me what it means.

    NGL it's a term I coined on a whim, but today, there are some companies hiring for that exact role.

    To me "AI Frontend Engineer" is a Frontend Engineer who specializes in building AI-powered products and experiences, similar to how video, audio, and meeting apps demand expertise beyond standard web development skills.

    The AI products you use on a daily basis — ChatGPT, Codex, Claude Code, n8n, Lovable, all involve a good degree of AI frontend engineering.

    Core frontend engineering: UI architecture, design systems, state management, routing, performance, a11y, etc.

    On top of the fundamental frontend skills, frontend engineers need to know thes:

    - LLM APIs: Streaming responses, tool calling, structured outputs, retries, cancellation
    - Agentic frontend experiences: Multi-turn conversations, approvalflows
    - UX patterns in AI apps: Awareness + how to implement them
    - Multimodal inputs: Text, file, image, audio, context attachment
    - Complex app architecture: AI orchestration layers, reusable components, message pipelines, artifact rendering
    - State management: Conversation history, streaming tokens, request states, errors

    A typical frontend engineer turns product requirements and backend APIs into a polished UI.

    An AI frontend engineer turns model capabilities into a polished, trustworthy, controllable product experience.

    If that interests you, follow me and join me on my journey of mastering AI frontend engineering.

      💡 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗮 𝘀𝗺𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗠𝗩𝗣 𝗼𝗳 𝗮 𝗥𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗹 𝗔𝘂𝗴𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗚𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 (𝗥𝗔𝗚) 𝗽𝗶𝗽𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲 - a one-night pull-off.

      The goal was clear:
      How can someone securely search across 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲 𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 - be it documents, copied text, or even websites and get meaningful answers without exposing private data?

      Here’s the approach I took:
      1. 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗲𝘅𝗶𝗻𝗴 → Split content into chunks + embeddings with 𝗟𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗶𝗻 utilities.
      2. 𝗩𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲 → Stored embeddings in QdrantDb (hosted in Docker on a VM).
      3. 𝗥𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗹 + 𝗟𝗟𝗠 → Fetch relevant chunks → grounded responses.
      4. 𝗡𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗯𝗼𝗼𝗸 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹 → Multiple notebooks with their own sources for contextual search.
      5. 𝗨𝗜 → Built with 𝘀𝗵𝗮𝗱𝗰𝗻 + 𝗩𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗲𝗹 𝗔𝗜 𝗦𝗗𝗞 for a conversational, source-aware experience.

      ✨ 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗶𝘁 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀:
      • Organizations and individuals deal with scattered information - across files, notes, and websites.
      • This pipeline allows them to 𝗼𝗿𝗴𝗮𝗻𝗶𝘇𝗲, 𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗽, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝗿𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗹𝘆.
      • Think of it as a step toward 𝘀𝗲𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗲, 𝗱𝗼𝗺𝗮𝗶𝗻-𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰 𝗰𝗼𝗽𝗶𝗹𝗼𝘁𝘀 that improve productivity without risking sensitive information.

      This is still an MVP, but it showed me how quickly an end-to-end workflow can come together.

      Would love to hear:
      👉 If you had this setup, what part of your business knowledge base would you want to make searchable first?
